topic: Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Combinations to Bases

outline.topic: Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Combinations to Bases

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Vectors as Arrows
sections.content: Briefly define vectors as directed segments in 2D space. Visualize them as movements: v = [2, 1] is 'go right 2, up 1'. Establish that scaling (c*v) and addition (v+w) form the building blocks of all operations.
sections.example: A delivery drone moving along vector A (North) and vector B (East).

sections.title: Linear Combinations and Span
sections.content: Define a linear combination as 'c1v1 + c2v2'. Introduce 'Span' as the set of all possible reach points. Use a grid animation: show the drone moving in varying steps of A and B, gradually filling the entire 2D plane.
sections.example: Two vectors A=[1,0] and B=[0,1] act as building blocks; by combining them, the drone can reach any point (x, y) on the map.

sections.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundant Vector
sections.content: Explain linear dependence visually: if vector C lies on the same line as A and B, it adds no 'new' dimensions. It is redundant. Use an animation showing a third vector being 'squashed' into the existing line.
sections.example: Three robots walking: Robot C follows the exact path of Robot A. If Robot A is already there, Robot C provides no new navigation capability.

sections.title: The Concept of Basis
sections.content: Define a Basis as the 'minimal set' of vectors that span the space without redundancy (linearly independent). Emphasize that a basis is the most efficient 'coordinate system' for a space.
sections.example: To describe a room, you need exactly 3 dimensions (Length, Width, Height). If you add a 4th measurement that is just a sum of the others, it's not a basis—it's redundant information.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Wrap up by linking the concepts: Vectors build Combinations -> Combinations create a Span -> Removing redundant vectors leaves us with a Basis. Connect back to the drone navigation example.
sections.example: A GPS system uses a basis of 3 satellites to pinpoint any position in 3D space. Adding a 4th satellite makes the system more robust but technically redundant for the base span.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Review: Vectors as Arrows
lecture_lines: Vectors are directed segments in 2D space.
Scaling and adding vectors build everything.
animations: Create two 2D arrows (vector v: #FF5733, vector w: #33FF57) at origin.
Fade in vector v from origin to coordinate (2,1). Label it 'v'.
Fade in vector w from origin to coordinate (-1,2). Label it 'w'.
Animate sum v+w as a new arrow (result: #3357FF) using parallelogram rule.
Highlight vectors v and w with glowing effect (#FFFFFF).

storyboard.title: Linear Combinations and Span
lecture_lines: Span is the set of all reachable points.
Vectors A and B fill the 2D plane.
animations: Display two vectors v (#FF5733) and w (#33FF57) in 2D space.
Animate scalar multiplication: scale v by 2 and w by -1.
Show the grid filling up as all scalar combinations are plotted.
Highlight the spanned plane in light blue (#00FFFF) with 30% opacity.
Animate a new vector u moving around the filled-in span plane.

storyboard.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundant Vector
lecture_lines: Linear dependence: redundant vector adds no dimension.
Vector C lying on line A, B is redundant.
Redundant vectors provide no new navigation.
animations: Display two linearly independent vectors v (#FF5733) and w (#33FF57).
Add a third vector u (#3357FF) lying perfectly on the line spanned by v and w.
Animate vector u fading out to show it provides no new span.

storyboard.title: The Concept of Basis
lecture_lines: Basis is the minimal spanning set.
Linearly independent vectors efficiently define space.
Basis is the most efficient coordinate system.
animations: Display two basis vectors i-hat (#FF5733) and j-hat (#33FF57) on axes.
Animate scaling and adding i-hat and j-hat to reach a point (3,2).
Fade in grid lines representing the basis coordinate system.

storyboard.title: Summary and Synthesis
animations: Show a summary table with concepts: Span, Dependence, and Basis.
Animate connections between these concepts via lines.
Fade out everything leaving only the title in center screen.
